newsitem.title: USA: Key IMM currencies end down amid firm U.S. assets.
newsitem.headline: Key IMM currencies end down amid firm U.S. assets.

text.p: Key IMM currencies finished lower, with March marks and Swiss francs near contract lows, as U.S. assets strengthened ahead of key U.S. employment data.

Traders said the dollar's bullish mood was back after having corrected from its lofty levels earlier this week. Traders said sinking Nikkei stocks buoyed the dollar versus yen and stronger than expected German joblessness weighed on marks.
Nervousness and pockets of thin trade were seen ahead of Friday's key U.S. data. December jobs are forecast to rise 192,000 and the unemployment rate is seen at 5.3.

"Basically, having tested support in the dollar early on it bounced off that to move higher," one IMM trading floor manager said. He said strength in March T-bond futures -- particularly after producer price data -- kept a lid on currencies.
December producer prices rose 0.5 percent overall and 0.1 percent in the core rate. Overall PPI was stronger than expected, but bond traders were cheered by the ex-food and energy reading.
Swiss and marks languished most of the session, with more downside Swiss franc potential seen, one trader said.

He pegged next support in Swiss at $0.7275. Mark support was seen at $0.6316, roughly 1.5900 spot. Traders were keeping a close eye on developments in the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who was hospitalized on Wednesday with the first signs of pneumonia. Traders said a weakened Russian presidency did not bode well for stability in the region.
March sterling posted moderate gains on the day, but remained confined in its recent range. March closed slightly below resistance at $1.6933 to $1.6940.
A barrage of comments from Federal Reserve Bank officials went largely unnoticed, as traders focused on rallies in U.S. stocks and bonds and positioning before Friday's data.

At settlement, March yen fell $0.000049 to $0.008672, marks fell $0.0014 at $0.6363, Swiss francs lost $0.0035 to $0.7341, sterling rose $0.0080 to $1.6928, the Canadian dollar was off $0.0001 flat at $0.7432, Australian dollar rose $0.0006 to $0.7801, and Mexican peso rose $0.000050 to $0.123275.
